title: Currency Netting & Hedge-Policy Challenge
shortTitle: Does the clever hedge earn its place?
question: Does a fitted currency hedge beat a simple 50% policy?
audience: Treasury, financial-risk and consulting analysts evaluating which currency exposures to cover and how to challenge a fitted hedge allocation.
data: Official H.10/FRED daily EUR, JPY, GBP, CAD and MXN quotations through October 23, 2026, with 25 values independently checked to the H.10 release. Monthly policy fitting uses completed months through 2022; January 2023-September 2026 is held out. All company cash flows, deal costs and budget locks are hypothetical.
methods: Normalize quotes to USD per foreign-currency unit, audit missing values without forward filling, and separate completed months from partial October. Net same-currency payments and receipts. Fit a constrained empirical adverse-cost CVaR policy on earlier months, freeze it and compare with uniform 50% coverage on 45 later months. Reconcile notional totals in SQL and replay cash costs independently in JavaScript.
findings: Within-currency netting reduces the hypothetical transaction base from $17.2 million gross to $6.8 million net, or 60.5%. On the later-month replay, the frozen fitted policy has an empirical 90% adverse-cost CVaR of $66,474 versus $85,969 for uniform 50% coverage, including an assumed charge. That is a historical diagnostic, not an achieved hedge result or future guarantee.
implications: Confirm which flows can legally settle together before hedging gross positions. Require a proposed allocation to beat a simple coverage rule on later observations, using actual execution costs before adoption. The historical result supports further investigation, not an implementation claim.
limitations: The budget-lock proxy freezes covered exposure at base spot; it is not a quoted forward or option. Rate differentials, collateral, credit, basis and bid-ask costs are omitted. Netting assumes same-currency, same-date settlement. Only 45 holdout months provide about 4.5 observations of tail mass. Current history may be revised; no real-time backtest, statistical superiority, actual savings or predictive coverage is claimed.
summary: A fitted hedge lowers the historical tail-cost diagnostic, but does it justify the complexity? Test it against uniform coverage after netting the cash flows that genuinely offset.

evidence.caption: Historical completed-month replay of hypothetical exposures and an assumed hedge charge. Lower empirical tail cost is preferable in this diagnostic; this is not actual hedge P&L or a future risk guarantee.
